extracted.intended_audience: mathematics educators, instructors, graders, and researchers in mathematics education (and advanced students interested in assessment of mathematical skill)
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-dimensional framework and rubric for assessing 'mathematical maturity' — the cognitive, behavioral, and emotional capacities that underpin doing and understanding mathematics (especially proofs). Intended to guide evaluation of students' work and the assumptions about audience sophistication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to move from specific examples to broad concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when a student elevates a pattern or instance to a valid general claim; penalize conflating an example with a general theorem. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstraction tolerance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to handle increasingly abstract ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures comfort with symbolic/axiomatic reasoning and moving away from concrete instances; observable in handling abstract definitions and arguments without pragmatic scaffolding. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of standard notation and acceptable mathematical style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses correct, consistent notation, conventional phrasing, and readability; includes choice of level of detail appropriate to audience. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding over memorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrable shift from rote learning to conceptual understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explanations that show conceptual links and reasoning rather than mere recitation of facts or procedures. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Key-idea separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to distinguish main ideas from routine bookkeeping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good work highlights central insights and relegates computation/routine steps to appropriate places; poor work gives equal weight to trivial steps. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric-analytic linking
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to translate between geometric, analytic, verbal, and symbolic representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates facility with multiple representations and switching between them to gain insight or provide justification. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-problem translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to convert a verbal problem into a mathematical formulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes identifying variables, assumptions, and appropriate mathematical model; important for applied tasks. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to recognize a valid proof and detect sloppy thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses whether a reader/student can judge whether an argument establishes its claim and spot gaps or unjustified steps. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitional precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to work with formal definitions precisely and appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes correct invocation of definitions, proper quantifier handling, and use of definitions to derive consequences. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection-finding
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to relate new material to existing knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for explicit references to prior results, analogous problems, or frameworks that situate new content; indicates integration of knowledge. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to assess one's own work for errors and gaps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes checking consistency, testing edge cases, and revisiting earlier steps when something fails. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolerance for results that take time and cognitive reorganization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed as willingness to pursue longer arguments, tolerate slow progress, and revisit failed approaches rather than abandoning them prematurely. (Source: Wikipedia consolidated list.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance for abstraction (Lew)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tolerance for abstraction (as emphasized in Lew's intellectual domain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lew's interviews highlight this as central: comfort staying at higher abstraction levels and moving among levels; note overlap with 'abstraction tolerance' above. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to follow technical arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to follow detailed, technical mathematical arguments (Lew — intellectual domain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated via comprehension tasks or oral questioning about chain-of-reasoning in proofs. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity for generalization (Lew)
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to generalize from examples or special cases to broader statements (Lew — intellectual domain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed by asking learners to extend arguments or conjecture general forms based on patterns. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of patterns across contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to perceive and apply patterns that recur in different mathematical settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for transfer of techniques or analogies between seemingly different problems. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patience with difficult problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral patience: sustained engagement with hard problems (Lew — behavioral domain).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observed as time-on-task and willingness to iterate; distinct from mere time spent if not productive. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence through false starts
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral persistence: ability to continue despite incorrect initial attempts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued as productive endurance; assess via process traces, journals, or logs showing revisions and iterative attempts. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to verify and re-verify
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral tendency to check one's work repeatedly and seek confirmation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes re-checking computations, testing special cases, and seeking alternative justifications. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multiple representations (Lew)
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral use of various representations (algebraic, geometric, numeric, verbal) to understand/solve problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses flexibility in choosing representations to simplify or illuminate a problem. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance for confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional tolerance for temporary uncertainty or not-knowing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured by tracking affective responses during tasks; mature learners use confusion productively rather than becoming discouraged. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Productive response to failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional resilience: treating failure as informative and adjusting strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for reframing errors as learning opportunities and explicit strategy changes after failure. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Comfort with not-knowing
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional comfort in admitting gaps and living with open problems during inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued in research contexts; assess through interviews and observed willingness to pose questions rather than fake knowledge. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleasure in intellectual struggle
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotional orientation: finding satisfaction in tackling difficult conceptual work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seen in voluntary engagement with challenging tasks and positive language about struggle. (Source: Lew, RUME 2019.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to follow a published proof and understand its structure and steps (proof-specific maturity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess via comprehension questions, paraphrasing, or reconstructing the argument. (Source: Proof-specific maturity section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to judge whether an argument is a valid proof and identify flaws (Selden & Selden).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes detecting logical gaps, hidden assumptions, or circular reasoning; can be measured with tasks asking students to evaluate sample proofs. (Source: Selden & Selden reference.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to produce original proofs of new claims (Weber's strategic knowledge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated by the student's ability to select strategies, plan approaches, and carry out correct derivations. (Source: Weber reference.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to adapt an existing proof to similar statements or changed assumptions (Avigad).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test by asking students to alter hypotheses or conclusions and adjust the proof accordingly; indicates deeper understanding. (Source: Avigad reference.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to identify errors and suggest improvements in proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes pinpointing unnecessary complications, suggesting clarifications, and proposing more elegant approaches. (Source: Proof-specific maturity section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof appreciation
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetic recognition of elegance, depth, or conceptual novelty in proofs (Inglis-Aberdein).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed via comparative judgment tasks or asking learners to explain why a proof is 'nice' or 'insightful'. (Source: Inglis-Aberdein reference.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability-Validity-Fluency (RVF) rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: An assessment tool for proof writing that examines readability, validity, and fluency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RVF to score student proofs on clarity of exposition, logical correctness, and ease of following the flow; useful for rubric-based grading of proof assignments. (Source: Assessment Methods.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative judgment for aesthetic dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Using comparative judgment (pairwise comparisons) to assess aesthetic qualities of proofs or solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better for subjective aspects like elegance; relies on relative judgments rather than absolute scoring. (Source: Assessment Methods.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral assessment for abstraction grasp
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of interviews or oral questioning following written work to probe conceptual understanding and abstraction tolerance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to reveal latent understanding not evident in written solutions; can check reasoning steps and meta-cognition. (Source: Assessment Methods.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification tasks as assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Tasks that require students to adapt or modify proofs to assess depth of understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask learners to generalize, specialize, or alter the statement/proof to see if they grasp the structure rather than merely reproducing steps. (Source: Assessment Methods.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizes appropriately (implied rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work generalizes to the right level — neither overgeneralizes nor undergeneralizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether generalizations are justified and proportionate; penalize unsupported leaps and trivial overfitting to examples. (Source: Implied Rubric section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Uses standard notation correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Correct and consistent use of conventional mathematical notation without causing confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for nonstandard symbols, inconsistent indexing, or notational abuses that impede comprehension. (Source: Implied Rubric section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguishes key ideas from bookkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Work separates the central conceptual moves from routine calculation or administrative steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good exposition highlights the main lemmas/insights and relegates mechanical work to appendices or brief mention. (Source: Implied Rubric section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Links representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Work shows ability to move among verbal, symbolic, and geometric representations and to use them coherently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess if the author translates intuition into formalism and vice versa to support understanding or proofs. (Source: Implied Rubric section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicates with precision in definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions are stated clearly and used precisely throughout the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for ambiguous quantifiers, unstated domain assumptions, and misuse of defined terms. (Source: Implied Rubric section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Shows patience (in presented work)
rubrics_metrics.description: The written work is not rushed — it neither skips crucial difficult steps nor hides essential reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mature piece will include enough work at critical points; evaluate whether omitted steps are justifiable given the intended audience. (Source: Implied Rubric section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Is self-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: The work demonstrates internal consistency checks, verification of claims, and spot-checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for sanity checks, limiting cases, or comments indicating the author tested or reflected on the result. (Source: Implied Rubric section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs of immaturity (negative indicators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observable signs that a piece (or author) is mathematically immature (consolidated negatives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes confusing an example with a general claim; non-standard or inconsistent notation; equal emphasis on key ideas and routine steps; failure to translate between representations; imprecise definitions; skipped steps at difficult points; and internal inconsistencies. Use these as red flags in assessment. (Source: Implied Rubric section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify assumed audience maturity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation must specify the assumed maturity level of the audience because what is acceptable to omit or leave implicit depends on it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rubrics should state the expected reader maturity (novice vs. expert); this determines acceptable terseness, completeness of proofs, and style. Assessors should not evaluate a text in isolation without this assumption. (Source: 'Why Maturity Matters' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust explicitness and style to audience maturity
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of detail, terseness, and style appropriateness should be judged relative to the intended readers' maturity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For mature audiences, terse and high-level exposition may be appropriate; for novices, more step-by-step explanation and explicit motivation are required. (Source: 'Why Maturity Matters' section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine what constitutes a 'complete' proof for intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide what gaps or omitted details are acceptable based on assumed reader maturity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same formal gap may be acceptable for experts but not for novices; rubrics should state completeness criteria aligned with audience expectations. (Source: 'Why Maturity Matters' section.)
